Please be very careful with the title. The first part sounds electronic, the second moves more toward house, and later there is a mixture of house with some jazz elements.

But what exactly do you mean by “Persian Jazz”? Adding a few jazz-influenced bass lines or elements to pop/electronic music does not automatically make the music jazz.

Actually, after the third part I started enjoying it much more because it moved closer to my own taste, which is house music. I liked the harmony, the combination of instruments, and especially how the track gradually became more progressive as a house track.

But calling it “Persian Jazz” is taking a risk. Imagine an academically trained jazz musician listening to this. The title could almost suggest that, among nearly 90 million Iranians, this is what represents Persian jazz. Is this really Persian jazz?

The music itself is nice and I enjoyed it. My criticism is not about the quality of the music; it is about the title and the musical classification. This is not jazz, and adding Persian elements does not make it “Persian Jazz.”

I think the track deserves a title that describes what it actually does well: electronic/house music with Persian influences and some jazz-inspired elements.

Thank you for such a thoughtful and detailed comment. I understand your point, and I agree that “Persian Jazz” should not imply that this music represents Persian jazz as a whole or jazz in the traditional or academic sense.

My intention was to describe a fusion: Persian-inspired melodies and atmosphere combined with electronic, house and jazz-influenced elements. However, I can see that the title may create a different expectation. “Persian electronic/house fusion with jazz-inspired elements” would certainly be a more precise description of this particular mix.

Genre boundaries can be fluid, but accurate classification is important. I genuinely appreciate your constructive feedback, and I’m very glad you enjoyed the harmony, instrumentation and progressive house direction of the later sections. Thank you for listening ❤❤
